headline: PHP flaws: Bangladesh Bank, land services, six banks’ websites remain offline

members.title: PHP flaws: Bangladesh Bank, land services, six banks’ websites remain offline
members.lead: The websites of Bangladesh Bank, the land services department and six banks remain offline due to a security vulnerability identified in PHP, a widely used programming language for website development. The websites have been temporarily taken down to avoid potential cyber risks and assess the security of their technological infrastructure. The websites were found offline at around 11:00am on Saturday. .PHP flaws prompt millions of hacking attempts amid rush to patch vulnerabilities. Bangladesh Bank has kept its website offline since Thursday. Following the central bank's move, several other banks also shut down their websites as a precautionary measure. The banks are Agrani Bank, Janata Bank, IFIC Bank, Standard Islami Bank, SBAC Bank and Bengal Commercial Bank. The banks concerned said the measure had been taken to avoid potential cyber risks and assess the security of their technological infrastructure. The websites will be restored once the security assessments and necessary measures are completed. . Meanwhile, in response to the PHP security vulnerability, the Ministry of Land has also taken its digital land services website offline for maintenance. .Websites shut down worldwide amid fears of cyberattacks: How prepared is Bangladesh?. According to an announcement by the ministry, the maintenance work is scheduled to continue for 36 hours, from midnight between Thursday and Friday until noon on Saturday. During this period, land services will not be available through the website land.gov.bd. . On 22 October, the government's cyber security agency, BGD e-GOV CIRT, issued an urgent alert regarding the PHP security vulnerability. It advised relevant organisations to identify the use of PHP on their servers, check whether the versions in use were vulnerable and take necessary security measures. members.title: What is PHP and why did it take government websites offline?
members.lead: Government websites across Europe went dark on Wednesday as operators raced to patch two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, one of the most widely used programming languages on the web. The developers of PHP said on Wednesday they would release patches for two critical vulnerabilities, and EU cybersecurity officials warned organisations unable to apply the fixes to take affected websites offline. Here is what you need to know: .Websites shut down worldwide amid fears of cyberattacks: How prepared is Bangladesh?. PHP is a programming language that runs websites. It works behind the scenes. When a user loads a page, the server running PHP assembles the content and sends the finished page to the browser. It is free, open source and maintained by volunteers. Site owners rarely interact with it directly. . PHP runs nearly 70 per cent of all websites whose programming language can be identified, according to web technology tracker W3Techs. It is the engine behind WordPress, the software that powers about 40 per cent of all websites such as blogs, small business pages, government portals, online shops and news sites. . The two vulnerabilities are rated 9.2 out of 10 on the CVSS v4.0 severity scale, a standard industry scoring system. CERT-EU, the European Union's cybersecurity response team, said that rating signals unauthenticated remote code execution, meaning an attacker can run commands on a vulnerable server, over the internet, with no password or account. .PHP flaws: Bangladesh Bank, land services, six banks’ websites remain offline. A single flaw in PHP opens the same door on millions of servers at once. Whoever exploits the flaw controls the website. GoDaddy, a web hosting provider, said that could mean stolen data, defaced pages or full-system compromise. Cloudflare's chief technology officer said early attacks were emerging.
